resolutions.researcher_notes: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, table 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (PDF p.78; printed p.75, the seed citation), lists 'Pump Station and A47/Yanbu | Saudi Aramco | 600 | 42/48/56' as an existing 2011 gas line. Listing in the in-service inventory supports operating. Live OPEC static-file URL now redirects to the OPEC homepage, so cited via Wayback snapshot (200). url_verifier flags substring-missing — the documented PDF text-extraction false-negative; content confirmed directly with pdftotext ('Pump Station and A47/Yanbu Saudi Aramco 600 42/48/56'). Single official source -> medium; status inferred from inventory listing, not stated literally.

The A47/Yanbu line appears in OPEC ASB2012's 'Gas pipelines' table (not the crude-oil table), directly supporting Fuel=Gas. Techint E&C (independent origin) describes the Shedgum-Yanbu link as a 'gas pipeline' to Yanbu in Saudi Arabia. Two independent sources agree on gas -> high.

OPEC ASB2012 gas-pipeline table gives length 600 (miles) for 'Pump Station and A47/Yanbu' = 965.6 km, matching GEM's 966.00 km (GEM converted mi->km). Single-source. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Techint and other sources describe the related Shedgum/Abqaiq-Yanbu gas/NGL line at ~1,166-1,170 km, materially longer than 966 km. Likely a naming/segmentation difference (A47-pump-station-to-Yanbu segment vs full Shedgum-Yanbu trunk), but the length figure is only corroborated by OPEC -> medium.

OPEC ASB2012 gas-pipeline table lists diameter '42/48/56' for 'Pump Station and A47/Yanbu', exactly matching GEM's Diameter='42, 48, 56' in. Single official source -> medium; no independent second source found reporting this multi-diameter figure for this line.

GEM records only StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia (no city endpoints filled). OPEC lists the line under Saudi Arabia, terminating at Yanbu (Red Sea, Saudi Arabia). Techint (independent) confirms the Shedgum->Yanbu gas line runs entirely within Saudi Arabia (Persian Gulf to Red Sea coast). Both endpoints unambiguously in Saudi Arabia -> high.

OPEC ASB2012 gas-pipeline table names 'Saudi Aramco' directly in the owner/operator column for 'Pump Station and A47/Yanbu', supporting Owner1=Saudi Aramco 100%. Consistent with Saudi Aramco being the sole owner of the kingdom's hydrocarbon trunk pipelines. Cited as single direct source (OPEC) -> medium; Techint article describes the build but does not name the owner.
